_doc: #1122 CRASH-SAFE BY DEFAULT, read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-crash-default-guard.py (crash-default-guard.yml, every push). Every fleet app gets the default crash handler (persist to files/crashes, the phone's local C3 WebServer sink, the remote upload, the crash screen) from libs:core's CoreInitProvider, with no code of its own. The guard fails when: libs:core stops installing CrashReports or stops depending on libs:crash (the module that holds the handler, the local sink and the generic crash screen); an app does not link libs:core (build.json modules, or its own settings.gradle(.kts) include); an app's own manifest names CoreInitProvider (tools:node=remove / enabled=false is an opt-out); an app's build.json sets crash_default to false; the C3 WebServer stops serving the sink route. `not_linked` lists the apps that do not link libs:core TODAY, each with its reason: it is a ratchet (an app NOT listed that stops linking core fails, and a listed app that links core now fails as stale until the entry is removed).

not_linked.ac_cloud-office: Cloud Office is a fetched upstream tree (web) with patches only: this repo holds no gradle project to include libs:core or libs:crash in, so there is no CoreInitProvider to install the handler. It joins when its android shell is vendored here (ticket #1122, on-phone follow-up).
